Name: Every CA inventoried (host, key and signature algorithms, validity, root or issuing); every template's configuration and permissions exported
Root of trust for device certificates decided (program D04)
If late (decisions): The root of trust is chosen without the CA inventory, so BYOCA can't be weighed against the hierarchy that exists

Name: Hardening checks (ESC1 to ESC8) run against templates, CA settings and PKI object ACLs; CA auditing on
Issued certificates inventoried by template with expiry; every relying party and the chains and CRLs it uses; strong-mapping sweep on every domain controller
Every template classified MIGRATE, BRIDGE, RETAIN or RETIRE against the template migration matrix
Critical and High hardening findings remediated and re-tested
Gate 1 — Assessed and hardened
Criteria (gates): Assessment approved by the PKI and CA administrators and the CISO and ISSO; no unclassified templates; every Critical and High finding remediated and re-tested (Chapter 03's migration gate); assessment record committed to the evidence repository

Name: Program starts the Cloud PKI design and issuing CA (start of P1.8)
If late (decisions): Under BYOCA, the root would sign a cloud issuing CA before its hierarchy passed the hardening gate

Name: Issuer for internal server certificates, and the lifecycle platform's edition
Options (decisions): Retained AD CS through the CLM platform, moving to a standalone issuing CA under the same root when the forest retires, and a public CA for names the internet trusts (Book 07's position); Certificate Manager, Self-Hosted, inside the boundary until a certificate-management package is FedRAMP authorized
If late (decisions): Server certificates keep renewing by hand, and the Data Platform plan's replacement-CA decision (D-D9) has no issuer to name

Name: Replacement CA for SQL Server's certificates decided (Data Platform D-D9)
Owner or approver: CIO and data leadership (Data Platform Identity Transformation plan)
If late (decisions): SQL Server's certificates are given an issuer before the PKI plan has named one

Name: Cloud PKI design done; issuing CA created (program P1.8)
If late (decisions): There's no cloud chain to export or deploy, and the foundation waits

Name: Full chain exported; CRL and AIA reachable over HTTP from where relying parties sit; LDAP-only AIA replaced; root CRL on a published schedule
Certificate Connector, current release, on its own servers wherever AD CS still serves SCEP or PKCS
Every CA that issues user certificates, and the Federal PKI chain for PIV, uploaded to the Entra trust store with its CRL URL
Trusted certificate profiles for the cloud chain and the federal root on managed devices; the chain to domain-joined relying parties; NTAuth only for logon issuers
Test certificate validated on every relying-party type; each CRL and AIA URL checked from inside, from the internet and in a test CBA sign-in
CLM platform deployed inside the boundary; its CA account scoped under the ESC7 review; Microsoft CA integration connected
Gate 2 — Foundation in place
Criteria (gates): Issuing CA active; trusted certificate profiles successful on at least 99% of managed devices; connector healthy; test certificate validated by every relying-party type; every CRL reachable from all three locations; the wave's rollback rehearsed in a test scope

Name: CBA method policy for PIV acceptance: the four settings, high-affinity bindings, the authentication strength, staged rollout for pilot users within its limits
Program starts CBA for PIV holders (start of P2.8)
If late (decisions): Pilot PIV holders are turned on for CBA before the method policy and bindings are set

Name: Program starts pilot certificate issuance (start of P2.7)
If late (decisions): Pilot devices receive certificates no relying party has been shown to accept

Name: Cloud PKI certificates issued; Wi-Fi and VPN verified (program P2.7)
If late (decisions): The pilot has nothing to observe, and Gate 3 waits

Name: Certificate-based authentication for PIV holders (program P2.8)
If late (decisions): Pilot users aren't on CBA, and Gate 3 waits

Name: Pilot observed: Intune certificate reports and Entra sign-in logs read; binding and authentication level confirmed; failures to the troubleshooting runbook
Gate 3 — Pilot authenticates with cloud certificates and CBA
Criteria (gates): At least 95% issuance success on pilot devices; no authentication failures caused by certificate configuration; pilot users on CBA at the intended authentication level; every pilot relying party accepts the cloud chain; AD CS autoenrollment still on for pilot devices

Name: Program G2 — Pilot Clean
If late (decisions): The program's pilot closes without the certificate pilot's evidence

Name: Device rings for SCEP and user populations for CBA
Options (decisions): Follow the program's rollout waves; by site, region or device tier. Dynamic groups built from governed attributes
If late (decisions): Production profiles can't be assigned, and Wave 4 waits

Name: Program starts rollout wave 1 (start of P3.1)
If late (decisions): The device rings have no divisions to follow

Name: SCEP profiles extended to production device groups, ring by ring, with the program's waves
PKCS and imported PKCS profiles for S/MIME and the remaining application certificates
Staged rollout extended to further user populations as sign-in data supports, within the 10-group limit
AD CS autoenrollment for MIGRATE templates removed on each ring once its devices hold valid cloud certificates
Server certificates (internal TLS, RADIUS, VPN gateways, SQL Server) discovered and enrolled for automated renewal; renewal owner recorded per class
Gate 4 — Every managed device on cloud certificates
Criteria (gates): Every managed device holds cloud-issued certificates for its MIGRATE use cases; every user intended for CBA on it; AD CS autoenrollment for MIGRATE templates removed on every migrated ring; server certificates renewing through the CLM platform

Name: Convert the federated domains to managed authentication, and in what order
Options (decisions): A test domain or the domain with the fewest users first, then the rest; hold a domain on federation as a dated exception
If late (decisions): AD FS stays in the sign-in path with certificate authentication on, and Gate 5 waits

Name: No unexpired AD CS certificates left on managed devices for MIGRATE use cases; federation settings recorded; AD FS backed up with Rapid Restore
Domains converted one at a time; staged rollout groups removed; AD FS certificate authentication off
AD CS procedures revised to BRIDGE and RETAIN scope only: domain controllers, LDAPS, NPS, server TLS
Gate 5 — Cut over
Criteria (gates): All target domains managed; AD FS certificate authentication off; CBA working for all users; no AD CS certificates on managed endpoints for MIGRATE templates; BRIDGE and RETAIN templates documented and running

Name: Rollback window: AD FS restorable but out of the sign-in path for 30 days; application use watched in Connect Health and the sign-in logs
Program starts moving user and device issuance off AD CS (start of P4.5)
If late (decisions): The program retires smart-card logon and AD CS issuance before the cutover has proved the cloud path

Name: User and device issuance off AD CS; smart-card logon GPO retired (program P4.5)
If late (decisions): MIGRATE-only components still issue, and decommissioning can't start

Name: Retire each MIGRATE-only AD CS component
Options (decisions): Retire, starting with the CA with the fewest dependents, once nothing depends on it; keep it as a dated exception under the hardening baseline
If late (decisions): NDES, CES/CEP and MIGRATE-only issuing CAs stay in service into the program's AD retirement

Name: Nothing depends on the CA, from the CLM inventory and the CA database; issuance stopped; events 4886 and 4888 read for a week
CA database and key backed up and archived; outstanding certificates revoked; the final CRL published to outlive them
Role services uninstalled before the CA role; the CA removed from the Entra trust store, Intune profiles and NTAuth
Decommission record committed; the archive's disposition set under the records schedule
Gate 6 — MIGRATE-only components retired
Criteria (gates): MIGRATE-only AD CS components retired or archived; offline root retained and documented, with the CA that signed the cloud issuing CA under BYOCA; no orphaned autoenrollment GPOs; HTTP CDP and AIA kept until the last certificate expires; decommission record in the evidence repository

Name: Program G4 — Legacy Quiet
If late (decisions): The program reaches Legacy Quiet with MIGRATE-only CAs still running
